description: We are a team of systems-thinkers, builders, and security-minded engineers who thrive in the terminal. From deploying local LLMs to orchestrating software, we specialize in building fast, deterministic, and scalable applications. We are bringing our deep understanding of backend infrastructure and open-source intelligence to the Space Apps Challenge to build solutions for Earth and beyond!!
summary:
Launchsmith is a browser-based 2D spacecraft engineering and flight simulator designed around NASA's iterative design-test-learn cycle. To address the challenge of spaceflight principles feeling abstract, the application transforms concepts like the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and atmospheric entry heating into an interactive mission loop. Players assemble landers, balance mission-critical parameters like mass, thrust, and budget, and navigate flight phases across five celestial bodies where their engineering decisions directly dictate survival.  
This project is important because it makes complex aerospace engineering and physics highly accessible through any web browser with no installation required. By matching in-game flight outcomes to historical NASA benchmarks—like the Mars Polar Lander and Galileo—and providing built-in engineering hints, Launchsmith bridges the gap between theoretical formulas and practical application. Ultimately, it delivers a powerful, gamified educational tool that supports both classroom instruction and self-paced learning.
details: Launchsmith is a browser-based 2D spacecraft engineering and flight simulator where players assemble landers from 19 parts and navigate ascent, transit, and descent phases governed by a physics engine utilizing the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation. Engineered as a React-based web application using Vite, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSX on an ASUS TUF Gaming F15 machine, the project aims to make complex aerospace concepts like rocket propulsion and entry physics accessible without requiring any software installation. By turning abstract formulas into an interactive design-test-learn loop supported by built-in engineering hints, it provides a significant educational impact for both classroom and self-paced learning. The game demonstrates creativity through a dynamic agency economy featuring launch fees and an R&D tech tree, alongside a hardware wear lifecycle where components visibly degrade across four states to force strategic repair-versus-replace decisions. Throughout development, your team carefully considered how to balance critical mission parameters like mass, thrust, and budget constraints, while maximizing player engagement by implementing four difficulty modes and matching flight outcomes to historical NASA benchmarks.
